title: FY2025 SNAP participation varies widely across states and DC
source_unit: USDA ERS state and District of Columbia population participation-rate observations
geography: United States; 50 states and District of Columbia

observations.period: FY2025; state and DC participation-rate distribution

denominator.unit: state and District of Columbia observations

minimum_state_rate.unit: percent of state/DC population receiving SNAP; Wyoming

maximum_state_rate.unit: percent of state/DC population receiving SNAP; New Mexico

median_state_rate.unit: percent; unweighted median of 51 state/DC rates

mean_state_rate.unit: percent; unweighted mean of 51 state/DC rates

state_rate_range.unit: percentage-point spread from minimum to maximum

observations.method: Direct transcription of the USDA ERS FY2025 chart-data workbook; summaries calculated across 50 states and DC without population weighting.
observations.uncertainty: The official chart supplies rates but not a comparable state-level decomposition of need, eligibility, administration, office/channel access, or take-up. The mean, median, and quartiles summarize the listed state observations rather than the US population.
observations.subgroup: State and District of Columbia population participation-rate observations; exact state values are preserved in the committed source layer.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high participation rate may reflect higher need or better take-up, while a low rate may reflect lower need or underaccess; state rates are not program-performance rankings or food-security measures.

related_sources.claim: USDA ERS page hosting the FY2025 state chart and national SNAP context.
Potential compatible state economic and demographic context for a future matched comparison; not joined in this record.

boundary: This record is a descriptive transcription and summary of 51 FY2025 state/DC participation rates. It does not establish why rates differ, whether eligible nonparticipants differ, state administrative performance, benefit adequacy, food security, household outcomes, trust, political action, or causal effects. Population-weighted national estimates and state-level need/eligibility/administrative decomposition remain open. The retrieval hash covers the committed state-specific layer.
